Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rendehR 1.0.0

First public release.

Changes from the internal builds

  • Antibiotics are a medication exposure, antibiotics_exp, in the duration concepts (rendehr_duration_concepts_config.csv) instead of the time-series concept antibiotics. Each order or administration keeps its start and gains its end and duration (prescriptions, MIMIC inputevents, eICU medication); doses are still stored in mg. Code that read antibiotics from the time-series tables should read antibiotics_exp from the duration tables.
  • The duration concept configuration is renamed from hddl_med_dur_config.csv to rendehr_duration_concepts_config.csv. A project override saved under the old name is no longer read; rename it.
  • import_cohort_icd_rbackend() and the source registry’s cohort_fn field are removed. Cohorts are selected by import_cohort_general(). ehr_add_source_assistant() and add_source_wizard() lose their cohort_fn and cohort_strategy arguments.

Cohorts and concepts

  • The bundled ICD diagnosis dictionary (d_icd_diagnoses.csv) is rebuilt from the public CMS ICD-9-CM (v23-v32) and ICD-10-CM (FY2016-FY2025) files by data-raw/d_icd_diagnoses.R. It covers every code of the previous dictionary except three ICD-9 category headers (780.0, V12.7, V58.1). Eleven retired ICD-9 codes in eICU diagnoses that were unmatched now resolve to ICD-9.

  • SCI stays are classified from their SCI codes only. A stay with any cord, cord-symptom or possible-cord code (is_sci 1, 3 or 999) is SCI, and its second level is traumatic, non-traumatic or unspecified depending on those codes. There are now six second-level categories instead of eight; the new scid_trauma_types column lists the trauma status of the SCI codes.

  • eICU medication tables keep their raw columns and add parsed mod_* columns (drug name, dose or rate, unit, start and stop) in medication_mod, infusiondrug_mod and admissiondrug_mod. Orders with a blank drug name (36 % in eICU 2.0) get their name from the drug code through rendehr_eicu_hicl_drugname_lookup.csv, which a file of the same name in the project config directory replaces. Infusion doses are now the charted rate, not the amount in the bag.

  • Some eICU exposure patterns match better: hydromorphone also matches the misspelling “Hydromorphine”, acetaminophen and hydrocodone no longer match chlorpheniramine, lepirudin matches its recombinant form, and linaclotide is no longer counted as sodium chloride.

  • eICU ionized calcium is labelled mg/dL throughout, but some hospitals report mmol/L under that label. The new conversion ca_ionized_by_value reads the unit from the value (up to 2 is mmol/L, 3.5 or more is mg/dL, the gap is left empty); about a quarter of eICU values were mmol/L wrongly divided by 4.

  • Calcium bounds follow ricu: 4-20 mg/dL for total and 0.5-2 mmol/L for ionized calcium (they were 0-10000). Bounds only affect opt-in range cleaning.

  • eICU FiO2 also reads the “FIO2 (%)” label; FiO2 has a lower bound of 20 %.

  • pH, INR, GCS and RASS carry a unit (pH, ratio, score) instead of the text 'NA'.

  • Hospital discharges to hospice are hospice in hospital_discharge_location (they were death; nearly all of these patients left the hospital alive).

  • Concepts without a unit (medication exposures, flags) store a missing unit instead of the text 'NA'.

  • The concept registry credits each concept’s origin: concepts defined by rendehR name the package, BlendedICU medication concepts cite its paper, and eICU derived concepts link the MIT-LCP eICU-CRD code. The time-series configuration no longer names PhysioNet as the origin.

  • ICD code columns of the clinical lookups (SCI list, injury causes, procedure classification, dictionaries) and of a user’s own ICD list are read as text, so codes with leading zeros such as 0331 keep them.

  • validate_concept_config() checks a concept configuration and lists each invalid row. The concept stage runs it first and warns once about every problem. Rows with an empty match_value or an unknown itm_class are skipped and named in the warning, and a missing user_concepts file stops the stage.

Loading data

  • load_merged_ts_wide() and fetch_concepts_wide() can drop values outside each concept’s plausible range before aggregating (clean = "range", bounds from the configuration or ranges =). Each concept gains an _n_cleaned column and the result a clean_report.
  • load_merged_ts(window_min = c(from, to)) keeps only rows in that window, filtered in the database, on the admission or ICU clock (window_ref).

Explorer

  • Cohort Explorer: Trajectories shows the median and IQR of a concept over the first hours or days of the stay by group; Compare puts two filter selections side by side with SMDs and outcome rates; Show R code gives the code that reproduces the current selection.
  • Concepts: Availability shows how many cohort admissions have each concept, Quality its units and values outside the plausible range, and the medication library adds exposure by day.
  • Subject Explorer: filters by age and admission type, the source definition of a clicked point, a second patient drawn dashed for comparison, and timed procedures on the timeline.
  • Every page has a help icon, the link icon reopens a view with its filters, and plots save as SVG.
  • run_explorer(cache_dir =) keeps the data bundle between runs, so later starts skip reading the merged tables. It is off by default because the file holds individual-level data.

Licence, documentation and interfaces

  • rendehR is now licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPL-3), the license of ricu, on whose concept definitions part of the concept layer is modelled. The MIT-licensed material it uses (MIT-LCP MIMIC-Code and eICU-Code SQL, the BlendedICU medication list) keeps its copyright notices in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

  • The documentation is now a set of tested articles: get started, projects and configuration, cohorts, the pipeline, harmonized data, concepts, the explorer, Sepsis-3 cohorts, the setup assistant, adding a source, and the MCP server. Every example was run on the open demo data; the vignettes are precomputed, so building the package renders stored outputs without a database or network.

  • The MCP bundle is version 1.0.0, the package version, with three skills (rendehr-user, rendehr-add-concept, rendehr-add-source) and nine read-only tools. Tool arguments must be a JSON object, numbers keep full precision, list_loaded_concepts reports the total, and cohort_summary errors when the source has no cohort tables.

  • The bundled example cohorts are scid (spinal cord injury, ICD list) and sepsis3 (Sepsis-3 SQL); the traumatic brain injury list (tbi) was removed.

  • The retired cohort entry points (import_cohort(), import_cohort_flex(), run_cohort_duckdb(), select_cohort_ids_duckdb()) have no aliases: use import_cohort_general(), materialize_cohort_duckdb() and select_cohort_ids().

  • drop_database() gains a confirm argument, so apps can pass the name the user typed; non-interactive sessions no longer wait at a console prompt.

  • New projects default to the "generic" cohort profile. Set cohort.profile = "scid" for the SCI reference implementation, which also turns on its clinical enrichment defaults.

  • The bundled SCI ICD dictionary is the v2.2.3 dictionary (scid_icds_rendehr.rds, the default; the CSV is the same table). It keeps the same codes and SCI/trauma flags, and describes location with anatomical_region and specific_level in snake_case. In cohort_info, scid_injury_level now holds the region ("cervical", "thoracic", …), scid_injury_location the coded level ("c5", "t11_t12", …), and the non-traumatic placeholder is "not_applicable".

  • cohort_summary() counts people rather than admission rows; SCI enrichment runs only for diagnosis-selected SCI cohorts; user SQL in subfolders of concepts_sqls/user is executed; ICU-level setup scripts build the cohort table at ICU grain; run_concepts() stops when a source’s raw modifications are missing; a relative base_dir resolves to an absolute path once; and a cohort selection plan prints its counts without the identifiers.

  • The cohort explorer (run_explorer()) has a simpler design and a rebuilt Setup page that configures a project for several sources and runs the pipeline stages for all of them, and a concept builder that drafts, previews and saves new or edited time-series concepts as a user_concepts file. Small-cell masking now also suppresses the cells and percentages from which a masked count could be recovered, and Kaplan-Meier curves use one index admission per patient.

rendehR 0.1.0

First labelled internal release. rendehR downloads, imports, cohort-filters and harmonizes ICU EHR data (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, eICU) into analysis-ready flat, time-series and duration tables, and merges sources into one schema.

Highlights

  • A cohort explorer (run_explorer()) with the logo’s brand theme: cohort overview (accrual, outcome heatmap, age pyramid, length of stay), Table 1 with SMDs, distributions, outcomes with Wilson CIs, Kaplan-Meier survival, long-term trends, cross-tabs, scatter plots, and a per-patient subject explorer that reads live time series and verifies source vs merged reads.
  • Management pages in the same app: Setup applies a project configuration on this machine and runs the pipeline stages as background tasks with live logs; Cohorts launches a cohort import (definition, ICD filter, ID list); Package manages libraries, sources, databases and exports.
  • An independent validation harness (the validation/ directory, kept on the dev branch only): demo and full-profile runs, including a concordance level against ricu; results and the findings register live in validation/Report.docx.
  • A local MCP bundle with three skills (inst/mcp, version 0.3.2).

Notes

  • Concept storage rounds unit-converted values to 3 decimals; raw values keep full source precision (value_raw). This rounding is a deliberate compatibility decision.
  • Vignettes in 0.1.0 were instructive only and used eval = FALSE. Since 1.0.0 they are precomputed on the open demos.
